sections.h2: Forestry mulching on Spring Branch ground
paras: Spring Branch sits along US 281 in western Comal County, north of Bulverde and west of Canyon Lake. The town takes its name from a spring-fed creek that flows into the Guadalupe River, and much of the surrounding land drains toward that river through steep, rocky draws.

Most Spring Branch property is thin soil over limestone. Ashe juniper fills in the slopes and fence lines, live oaks gather in mottes, and brush closes the gaps between them. Forestry mulching suits that ground because the mulcher grinds vegetation in place and leaves the thin topsoil where it lies.

sections.h2: Choosing a mulcher for river slopes and open pasture
paras: A single Spring Branch tract can change character from one end to the other. Flat pasture near the road can drop into a cedar-choked draw a short walk later. We match the machine to the ground.
bullets: Compact track machines handle tight access, slopes and uneven ground.
Large articulated wheel machines bring high horsepower and high production to open ground.
Smaller machines cover about half an acre to an acre in an 8-hour day. Larger machines cover about 1 to 3 acres a day with reasonable tree coverage.
Our equipment includes a CAT 275 compact track loader and a Weiler M860A mulcher.

sections.h2: The mulch finish and how fast grass returns
paras: Forestry mulching from 9 Arrow leaves a fine finish. Our crews call the small material toothpicks or hamster chips. A fine finish looks better, is easier to drive over, and lets grass regrow faster than a coarse one.

Grass under a light layer of mulch can green up within days after a rain. Where heavy timber leaves mulch up to 12 inches deep, regrowth can take 2 to 3 years. If you want less material on the ground, the mulch can be stockpiled or hauled off.
Root balls stay in the ground with mulching, which keeps soil stable on Spring Branch slopes. Dozing disturbs that soil and raises the risk of erosion.

sections.h2: Old brush piles, building sites and the rest of the job
paras: If your Spring Branch property carries old brush piles, including bulldozer piles as large as a house, we mulch them in place instead of burning them. Burning is often prohibited during burn bans anyway. Our [brush clearing](brush-removal) page covers overgrown lots and leftover piles in more detail.

Planning a house or barn? [Land clearing for a building site](site-prep) adds grubbing with dozers and excavators where root balls have to come out, such as under a foundation, and we mulch those root balls on site.

For the full service, see [forestry mulching in Central Texas](forestry-mulching-and-land-clearing). Neighbors just south and east can read about [forestry mulching in Bulverde](forestry-mulching-bulverde-tx) and [forestry mulching around Canyon Lake](forestry-mulching-canyon-lake-tx). We treat your land as if it were our own. It does not get better.

faqs.q: Can a forestry mulcher work the steep slopes near the Guadalupe River in Spring Branch?
faqs.a: Yes, forestry mulching works on the steep ground around Spring Branch when the machine fits the slope. Compact track machines are built for slopes, tight access and uneven ground. Steep, rocky draws take longer than open pasture, and that difference is built into the estimate before any work starts.

faqs.q: Do I need to burn anything after forestry mulching in Spring Branch?
faqs.a: No burning is needed after forestry mulching in Spring Branch. The mulcher grinds trees and brush where they stand, so there are no burn piles to manage and nothing to haul away. That helps during burn bans, when burning is often prohibited. The ground is left covered in fine mulch.

faqs.q: How big a tree can forestry mulching take down in Spring Branch?
faqs.a: Forestry mulching in Spring Branch has no tree size limit, from light regrowth up to large hardwoods and mature trees. Machine size changes the time it takes. A tree that needs an hour on a smaller machine can take as little as 15 minutes on a large, high-horsepower machine.

faqs.q: Can you mulch around the live oaks I want to keep in Spring Branch?
faqs.a: Yes, selective forestry mulching in Spring Branch takes the cedar and brush and leaves the live oaks you want to keep. Drought stress and oak wilt are common in Central Texas, and selective clearing is often the best option to protect healthy trees growing near ones that are already declining.
